title: If There Were More Lines: Hypotheticals about Energy

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si* with the imperfect subjunctive from B1 Unit 4, for an imagined situation, and the conditional for the result (*Si fuera tú, hablaría con el profesor*). The debate about energy in Chile is full of "what if" thinking.

sections.title: Imagining other conditions
rows: Si hubiera más líneas, se aprovecharía mejor la energía solar.
*si* + *hubiera* + conditional: there are not enough lines now
Si Chile exportara hidrógeno verde, ganaría dinero.
*si* + *exportara* + conditional: Chile does not export it yet
Si soplara menos viento, se produciría menos hidrógeno.
Si cerraran las centrales, bajaría la contaminación.
*si* + *cerraran* + conditional: the plants are still open

items.spanish: Si hubiera más líneas de transmisión, se aprovecharía mejor la energía solar del norte.
items.english: If there were more transmission lines, the solar energy of the north would be used better.

items.spanish: Si Chile exportara hidrógeno verde, ganaría más dinero.
items.english: If Chile exported green hydrogen, it would earn more money.

items.spanish: Si hubiera más viento, se produciría más hidrógeno.
items.english: If there were more wind, more hydrogen would be produced.

items.spanish: Si cerraran las centrales de carbón, bajaría la contaminación.
items.english: If the coal plants closed, pollution would fall.

sections.content: Never put the conditional after *si*: say *si exportara*, not *si exportaría*. The imperfect subjunctive after *si* does not talk about the past: it imagines something that is not true now.
